scale_magnet_temperature.reading: B_r(T) = B_r(T_ref)·(1 + α·(T − T_ref)), T_ref in the (23 ± 5) °C band a unit meets its class minimum at; a period fixed for the batch must keep the weakest unit over the need at the hottest hour and the strongest inside the range at the coldest. A family holds a cell when its strongest class (MAGNET_FAMILIES_BR_T, the 2001/AMD1:2004 minima) reaches the minimum, over a continuous period inside its thermal cap, of the hot-end need; «with the unwrap floor» adds P ≥ the cross-season unwrap period and lets any class of the family's span be chosen. Kind = a uniform batch meeting its minimum at 28 °C, the coefficient's smaller end, 78's α 0.5 hour and the coldest air; adverse = the need on a unit meeting its minimum at 18 °C and the cap on one meeting it at 28 °C, the larger end, 78's α 0.9 hour and 81's sky edge that hour. Gap and thickness limits are solved roots (None = no gap ≥ 0.2 mm / no thickness; the t → ∞ need beside), for the offset and range bounds. The class minima are valid only for magnets ≥ 5 mm in all three directions (IEC 60404-8-1:2023 §5.2) — every thinner scale, and every pole shorter than 5 mm (P/2 at the caps here is under it), reads them outside that validity. Ferrite has no coefficient: it is solved isothermally, and its floor list is its own. The 2015 and 2023 editions' minima are unread: `remanence_a_class_must_reach_T_unread_editions` is what such a class would have to reach.

sensor_table.rule: the SUM rule: per temperature branch the offset term (P/2π)·δB_pair/B plus the mismatch term (P/2π)·ε/2, both per kelvin, must stay within the frames' 0.3 µm/K — a linear sum of two worst-case bounds of independent sources (an RSS would be kinder and is not taken); δB_pair = √(δa² + δb²) of the pair's axes; each branch over its own band, where that band's field is weakest — 25 → +125 °C at the hottest hour, 25 → −40 °C at its warm end, 25 °C (at the cold edge the field is stronger) — and the range at the coldest hour; the guaranteed column (the mismatch's typical one where no guaranteed one exists, flagged). The support's term (1) is NOT summed — it is a maximum over unknown fixations

sensor_drift_linearity.verdict: LIN bounds the SIZE of the drift's residual over −40…+125 °C, not its slope (TI: not a per-kelvin coefficient), so the frames' per-kelvin rule has no guaranteed reading from it; at the window's edge — the most favourable point — the readings hold 3 mm on REFeB in 10 of 72 row·pair·corner·reading cells, every one with the offset compensated; nearer 25 °C the same residual is a larger per-kelvin figure without bound, and the drift's repeatability and 20-year stability are not published — a linear compensation is a MEASURED band, not a guarantee. The offset row has two readings of what LIN is a share of: TI's follow-up (2026-11-18) — the total offset drift over the full range, a best-fit line not held to 25 °C — holds 3 mm on REFeB in 19 of 24 of its cells, 8 with the unwrap floor; TI's answer excludes a share of the full-scale range, and our full-scale reading is kept as the adverse bound (its residual is ×47–×160 TI's, whose own is ×15–×24 below one read's noise): on the same line it holds in 4 of 24, 4 with the floor. With that line not through 25 °C the offset's «from 25 °C» cells are a control — 6 of the 10 holds above; without them 4 of 48

unwrap.basis_note: season-consistent: winter = the frost swing with no growth; growing season = a month of the fast end's increment (laid down over ≥ 4 months — our assumption; a growing-season outage of a month is itself an assumption, 110's outages fall in winter) plus the daily swing; cross-season = an outage spanning both. P/2 bounds an absolute-in-period phase; the collector's «half a pole» bounds an incremental pole counter, a different reader. A period above P* buys unwrap margin at a small cost to the OFFSET term (its optimum is flat) — the angle and mismatch errors grow in proportion to P.
unwrap.count_home: the server unwraps the delivered phases — nothing persisted on the device (03_01: the RTC backup domain does not survive an outage on our board). What breaks it: a maintenance event that moves the sensor against the scale (radome off/on, a board re-seat) — a step the server must mark as a discontinuity; a ledger whose old readings are archived or expire — the server keeps a persisted running unwrapped position, not a recompute over history; creep of the sensor's mount; and the phase needs a field on the wire.
